\chapter{Writing --- Your Own Line}
\label{ch:escribir-frase-propia}
\hlchaptermodality{337}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can write a greeting and my name from a closed supply of known words, choosing the greeting the hour asks for.}

Complete ES-W01-frase-propia: with no model to copy, choose one of four greetings by the hour and order it in front of me llamo.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[buenos días]{Your own line — the first writing with no model}

\label{lesson:ES-W01-frase-propia}



\begin{quote}
You have written \textbf{hola} four ways: traced, copied, copied from memory, and written from a sound alone.

Every one of those had something to reach for. This one does not.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
Here is your whole supply. Nothing outside it may go on the page.

\begin{quote}
\emph{hola} · \emph{buenos días} · \emph{buenas tardes} · \emph{buenas noches} · \emph{me llamo}
\end{quote}

Now the situation. \textbf{It is four in the afternoon, and you are meeting someone for the first time.}

Write two things, in this order: the greeting the hour asks for, and your name.

Two decisions live in that. Which of four greetings the clock allows — and what has to come first so a stranger knows who is talking. Nobody is supplying either one. That is what makes this different from every writing step before it: the words are old, and the choosing is new.

Write it now, then read on.

Your line should be \textbf{Buenas tardes. Me llamo} and then your name. If you reached for \emph{buenos días}, check the hour again. If the name came first, read it back aloud and hear how the greeting wants to open the door.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} your own line back to yourself, and hear that it is a real thing to say
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What did you supply that no earlier writing lesson asked for? (The \textbf{choice} — which words, and in what order.)

Nothing on your page was new Spanish. The step is that you decided where each old word went. Next: the same skill on a longer answer, the kind a form asks for.
\end{tcolorbox}
